subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal first, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat/heartbeat retry parity before treating it as fixed?
rationale: Current source shows both a shared conflict throw and surface-specific terminalization paths, while the proof-positive open PR changes the session lifecycle recovery boundary.

options.title: Review shared self-heal first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the canonical fix candidate, then retest WebChat and heartbeat after it lands.

options.title: Require surface retry parity
options.body: Keep the shared PR separate and require explicit WebChat/heartbeat retry or spool handling before this issue can close.

options.title: Ask for more live surface proof
options.body: Request a current-main WebChat or heartbeat reproduction before choosing between shared recovery and surface retries.

recommendation.title: Review shared self-heal first
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the canonical fix candidate, then retest WebChat and heartbeat after it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history on the guarded reply-session initialization boundary where this owner-boundary decision sits.
